title: Throughput economics & p95 latency scan - Solaris Systems
next_steps: Share benchmark template and sample payloads
Schedule Dedicated-hosted probe run w/ Solaris infra (week of 2027-07-05)
Send SOC2 + network topology checklist and Dedicated sizing deck
action_items: Ravi Patel: run synthetic tokens/sec + streaming p95 probe (8k context, 3 concurrency tiers) by 2027-07-02
Alicia Gomez: provide 90-day anonymized traffic trace and 5 representative prompt families by 2027-07-01
Maya Chen: email Dedicated vs Hosted cost/sla comparison + baseline benchmark results by 2027-06-30
header:
Date: 2027-06-28 | Time: 09:00 PT | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Ravi Patel (Redwood SE); Alicia Gomez (Solaris CTO); Ethan Marsh (Solaris Platform Eng); Dr. Lena Park (Solaris ML Infra)
summary: Discovery focused on p95 latency SLOs, concurrency expectations for streaming tokens/sec, and trade-offs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC) for Solaris. Agreed to run three probe profiles and share traffic + prompts. Key concerns: stable p95 under burst, AVX/quantization impact, and egress/network hops in VPC setups.
topics: p95 latency targets and measurement methodology
Next steps for probes and data share
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Alright thanks everyone for joining, we got about 45 minutes so we'll cover your p95 goals, typical traffic, and then map a small probe plan — I'm Maya, AE on the account.
[00:08] Alicia Gomez: Hi Maya, hi Ravi, thanks. We're short on time but have a pretty specific ask: can Redwood hit p95 <= 250ms for streaming token  when 3 concurrent sessions per user at peak? that's our mobile assistant SLO.
[00:20] Ravi Patel: quick clarifying q — is that 250ms per token or for entire response?
[00:24] Alicia Gomez: good call — p95 per token for the streaming chunks (we measure server token emisson), overall resp can be higher.
[00:30] Ethan Marsh: And our typical prompt lengths are like 250 tokens, but with context up to 6k for retrieval augmented cases.
[00:36] Dr. Lena Park: also we have frequent multi-turn, so KV cache reuse is important, we want p95 not to spike with 6k context.
[00:42] Maya Chen: understood. high-level — hosted API can often hit low single-digit token latencies on small contexts, but p95 at long contexts and continuous streaming can vary; Dedicated with reserved GPUs helps stabilize that. We'll run profiler probes to validate.
[01:00] Ravi Patel: I'll add that kernel selection and quantization change the per-token time. If you use int8 or q4, you'll save cost but might add a small per-token overhead in some runtimes.
[01:10] Alicia Gomez: we prefer lower cost but not at the expense of unpredictable p95 spikes. our decision leans to predictable worst-case.
[01:18] Maya Chen: that's a classic tradeoff. to be concrete, can you share your 90-day request rate? average rps and peak concurrent users?
[01:25] Alicia Gomez: average 120 rps, peak 1.2k rps, roughly 800 concurrent streaming sessions across regions at peak.
[01:33] Ethan Marsh: regional split is 70% NA, 20% EU, 10% APAC.
[01:38] Maya Chen: good — that helps with routing/region placement. for Dedicated we'd propose a pool sized for sustained throughput plus some burst capacity; for Hosted we can route to multi-node fleet but SLOs are probabilistic.
[01:50] Ravi Patel: question for Lena — are you doing strict token-level streaming (1 token at a time) or micro-batch streaming? that affects throughput and network overhead.
[01:57] Dr. Lena Park: micro-batches of 8 tokens is our current plan, doc assistant uses small batches to reduce chattiness.
[02:03] Maya Chen: perfect. micro-batches = fewer network hops. we should test both 1-token and 8-token batching in probes.
[02:10] Alicia Gomez: on security — for Dedicated/Private we need KMS integration and audit logs retained 1 year. do you support HSM-backed keys?
[02:18] Maya Chen: yes we integrate with customer KMS and HSM in Private deployments; Dedicated can be configured to use customer-managed keys for model payload encryption at rest. we'll send SOC2 and KMS doc links.
[02:27] Ethan Marsh: what about egress hops in a VPC peering set-up? last vendor we used had double NAT adding 60-80ms.
[02:34] Ravi Patel: good flag. network egress and NAT can dominate p95 if not tunneled properly. For Private we recommend colocated inference nodes in the same VPC to avoid that. we'll include network checklist.
[02:43] Alicia Gomez: nice. how do you measure p95? are you measuring server-side token emit time or end-to-end to client?
[02:50] Maya Chen: we typically record server-side per-token emit times plus end-to-end in the console via a synthetic agent. For your SLO we should measure both, but p95 per-token server-side is first step.
[02:59] Dr. Lena Park: can Redwood's console show per-route p95 broken down by model variant and quantization?
[03:04] Maya Chen: yes, per-route/model breakdowns are in Console; we can show quantization and kernel-level filters too.
[03:10] Ravi Patel: okay next — probe profile. propose three profiles: 1) short context (512) high QPS baseline, 2) long context (6k) moderate QPS with streaming micro-batches, 3) simulated burst with 1k sessions ramp over 30s. each run 10 minutes per ramp stage.
[03:25] Alicia Gomez: sounds good. for long context, you guys handle KV cache warms?
[03:30] Ravi Patel: we'll simulate cache warm and cold scenarios; cache cold tends to spike latency. We'll instrument cache hit rates and show p95 delta.
[03:36] Ethan Marsh: how do you handle fallback if a node is overloaded — do you have automatic fallback to smaller models?
[03:41] Maya Chen: yes we support routing policies with automatic fallback to compatible model variants (smaller quantized variant) and region fallback. that's in the rollout config.
[03:49] Alicia Gomez: ok important: any consistency or signature differences between fallbacks? we rely on certain output formats.
[03:54] Ravi Patel: function calling and structured outputs are preserved generally but you'll want to run evals — small model variants can introduce regressions. we'll include quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to your prompt set.
[04:05] Maya Chen: to follow up, we'll need sample prompts and a small eval harness so we can run quality checks during bursts.
[04:10] Dr. Lena Park: we can provide 5 categories: short Q&A, code assist, summarization, retrieval + answer, multi-turn conversation.
[04:19] Maya Chen: perfect. cost discussion — Alicia, you said economics matter; do you have a cost target per 1k tokens or per-API call?
[04:25] Alicia Gomez: we model cost per active session per hour; rough budget: <$0.50 per active session-hour at peak. translate that to per-token later.
[04:33] Ravi Patel: we can run cost sims. Dedicated usually has a lower per-token cost at scale but with reservation commitments; Hosted is more flexible but can be higher under sustained load.
[04:43] Ethan Marsh: curious about quantization impact — can we run one probe with q4 and one with fp16?
[04:48] Maya Chen: yes. we'll compare q4_0, int8-ish profiles and fp16; show throughput, latency, and token quality regression.
[04:55] Alicia Gomez: thank you. also, how do you handle autoscale cold-starts? our traffic is spikey with short bursts.
[05:01] Ravi Patel: for Dedicated we offer pre-warmed burst nodes and configurable autoscale policies with warm buffer; for Hosted it's a best-effort fleet with autoscale latency trade-offs. pre-warm reduces cold start p95 spikes.
[05:12] Dr. Lena Park: do you have a way to simulate client backpressure? we sometimes need to shape server-side emission rate to avoid client overload.
[05:18] Maya Chen: we support token throttling and per-connection rate limits; you can control emission and windowing in the SDK.
[05:24] Alicia Gomez: nice. one more on metrics — can we get per-token CPU/GPU usage and kernel breakdown? that would help our infra team.
[05:31] Ravi Patel: yes, our trace hooks can export per-token kernel times and GPU occupancy; we'll share a sample trace export format.
[05:37] Maya Chen: ok next — timeline. if you want to run probes the week of July 5, we'll need prompts and traces by July 1. Then Ravi will coordinate probe runs and we aim to deliver a baseline report by July 8.
[05:48] Alicia Gomez: that's workable. if Dedicated looks good we'll request a proof-of-concept with a 3-month reserved pool.
[05:55] Maya Chen: excellent. any blocker on security/process?
[05:59] Ethan Marsh: procurement wants SOC2 + contract redlines; legal will need our standard DPA.
[06:04] Maya Chen: we'll send SOC2 and the standard redline-friendly contract template.
[06:08] Dr. Lena Park: small nit — when you do probes, can you run with our synthetic agent located in our EU region to catch routing surprises?
[06:14] Ravi Patel: yes we'll deploy a probe runner in EU and NA. good catch.
[06:18] Alicia Gomez: competitor question — we run a quick POC with VertexCloud; they hit good median but p95 was all over the place during bursts. how is Redwood different?
[06:26] Maya Chen: our main differences are (1) kernel-level optimizations and continuous batching in the runtime, (2) dedicated pools to avoid noisy neighbors, and (3) smart routing plus automatic fallbacks. But we need probes to prove it for your workload.
[06:37] Ethan Marsh: do you have examples of customers with similar concurrency patterns?
[06:40] Maya Chen: yes, we have a healthcare customer (anonymized) with 700 concurrent streaming sessions and strict p95; we can share anonymized runbook and metrics.
[06:47] Dr. Lena Park: ok let's talk specifics for the probe plan now.
[06:51] Ravi Patel: Probe A: Baseline 512 ctx, 8-token micro-batch, ramp to 200 rps, steady 10 minutes. Collect server-token p95, GPU occupancy, and end-to-end. Probe B: Long context 6k, cache warm/cold phases, 300 rps. Probe C: Burst test, ramp 0->1k sessions over 30s, hold 3 minutes, monitor p95 tail and fallback triggers.
[07:17] Alicia Gomez: for Probe C, please instrument fallback events and percent of requests that saw model downscale.
[07:22] Ravi Patel: will do. we'll also record model variant latency delta and quality regression stats.
[07:27] Maya Chen: I'll ask SE to run the initial Hosted run and then rerun on a Dedicated reserved pool to show differences.
[07:34] Alicia Gomez: good. on the data side, can Redwood consume our traffic trace as anonymized JSON?
[07:39] Maya Chen: yes, JSON trace is preferred; please strip PII. We'll provide a small schema.
[07:44] Ethan Marsh: logistic q — do you require VPC peering for Dedicated?
[07:48] Ravi Patel: for Dedicated we recommend VPC peering/PrivateLink for lowest latency. Private deployments can be fully customer-controlled.
[07:54] Alicia Gomez: anything we miss? I want to ensure the report calls out recommended Reserved capacity and expected cost per active session-hour.
[07:59] Maya Chen: we'll include both cost sims and recommended Reserved capacity with burst buffer.
[08:03] Dr. Lena Park: can we get a small sample of the console p95 dashboard earlier? just a screenshot or sample CSV?
[08:09] Maya Chen: yes, we'll send screenshots and a sample CSV from our last benchmark.
[08:13] Ethan Marsh: timeline recap please.
[08:15] Maya Chen: sure — Maya to share SOC2, network checklist, and Dedicated vs Hosted sizing deck by 2027-06-30. Alicia to share prompts and trace by 2027-07-01. Ravi to run probes the week of 2027-07-05 and deliver baseline report by 2027-07-08.
[08:30] Alicia Gomez: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[08:33] Maya Chen: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the probe kickoff and include the config template link: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/solaris-template
[08:40] [End of recording]
